answers.rationale: Inline diffs are exactly what I need to feel confident about multi-file changes. Being able to see exactly what changed before accepting gives me the control I want without sacrificing the speed benefit of an agent.
Checkpoint rollback is a game-changer for me. Knowing I can undo autonomously if something goes wrong removes my biggest hesitation about letting an agent handle complex refactoring or feature work.
My main worry is that the agent could make logically incorrect changes that pass a diff review but break functionality downstream. Subtle logic errors are harder to catch than obvious syntax issues.

answers.value: Refactoring variable names and updating imports across a module with existing test coverage
answers.rationale: This feels safe because the changes are mechanical and low-risk—tests will immediately catch if something breaks. It's a good way to build trust in the tool before delegating more complex tasks.
